scope: R3 / UNINST-01 item 350: a managed link whose target disappeared can be identified and cleaned up, instead of leaving the entry permanently stuck
status: implemented-and-isolated-verified; no real user environment touched
gapClosed: preview_uninstall_scope treated an unresolvable link target as a blocker: canonicalize() failing on the target set scope_complete=false and pushed a 管理链接目标 blocked entry. The consequence was the opposite of the intent — the one kind of environment that actually needs repair (a dangling managed link) was the one the app refused to touch, and the user had no way to clear it.

implementation.separation: Two different failures were conflated. 'link_target_path' failing means the link object itself is unreadable, and that still blocks. 'canonicalize' failing on an already-read target means the destination is gone while the object is intact — that is now tracked separately as unresolved_target.
implementation.preview: An unresolved target produces a removable entry named 失效链接入口 whose text states that only the link object is removed and that no target is ever followed or deleted. It does not claim to retain a 受管目标目录, because that directory no longer exists.
implementation.execution: No new removal path was needed: link_ownership already opens the link object with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT and marks that handle for deletion, so it never resolves the target. The fixture proves this end to end rather than assuming it.

fixtures.name: commands::tests::a_dangling_managed_link_can_be_cleaned_up_instead_of_blocking_forever
asserts: after the target directory is deleted the link object still exists
the preview reports scope_complete=true and pushes no 管理链接目标 blocker
a 失效链接入口 entry appears with the '不会跟随或删除任何目标' promise
the preview does not pretend to retain a 受管目标目录 that no longer exists

fixtures.name: commands::tests::a_dangling_link_is_removed_without_touching_anything_else
asserts: execution returns VerifiedScopeRemoved with no failures
the link entry is gone afterwards
the target path is not recreated by the removal

notVerified: The dangling target was produced by deleting a temporary fixture directory, not by uninstalling a real runtime
A link whose target is unreadable because of permissions (rather than absent) takes the blocking path; that case was not re-exercised here
No UI change was needed, so no new UI assertion covers the 失效链接入口 row
limitations: This covers dangling link entries only. A corrupted plain directory (no link) still relies on the existing broken-status reporting; there is no separate repair action for it
The 重新识别 half of item 350 is unchanged: the overview already re-reads structure and version on every scan, but there is no dedicated 'repair' affordance beyond this removal path
Removal is the only offered repair. Re-pointing a dangling link at a new target would be an implicit move, which the plan explicitly forbids
